answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism where identities must bid for limited slots. Each new identity raises the auction cost by 10%, with bids starting at $100 and quickly escalating to $1,000 or more. Each participant must also stake tokens equal to their bid, immobilizing funds, while established agents vouch for them As a raven's call echoes over an ocean, the costs pile up, generating a whisper of desperation among attackers. Ultimately, the financial burden becomes unsustainable, deterring the creation of fake identities.
